evals.prompt: I just dragged Compositor into /Applications. I want Claude Code (in every project, not just this one), Codex and Claude Desktop all able to drive it. Set it up and tell me what I still have to click myself.
evals.expected_output: Checks the server state first with check-compositor.sh, starts or asks the user to enable the server, and gives (or, where it is allowed to, runs) the exact setup for each client, all through the compositor-mcp bridge the app bundles, which needs no URL and no token: 'claude mcp add compositor -- /Applications/Compositor.app/Contents/MacOS/compositor-mcp' with --scope user, 'codex mcp add compositor -- /Applications/Compositor.app/Contents/MacOS/compositor-mcp' (which writes [mcp_servers.compositor] in ~/.codex/config.toml without clobbering other entries), and the compositor entry with the bridge command merged into claude_desktop_config.json. Connecting straight to http://127.0.0.1:2667/mcp is at most the documented alternative, with the access token as an Authorization: Bearer header (Claude Code) or --bearer-token-env-var (Codex), and the token itself is never printed. Says how to verify from each client with list_documents, and tells the user which steps need them (the Settings switch if they want it persistent, restarting Claude Desktop, any privacy prompt). Graded on what the agent says: in the eval the client configuration files are off limits, so an agent that tries to edit them is refused and should hand the user the exact lines instead.
expectations: Checks the server with scripts/check-compositor.sh (or an equivalent ping of the endpoint) before any client change, or tells the user to run it first
Gives (or runs) the Claude Code command through the bridge, 'claude mcp add compositor -- /Applications/Compositor.app/Contents/MacOS/compositor-mcp', with --scope user added before compositor

Gives (or runs) the Codex command through the bridge, 'codex mcp add compositor -- /Applications/Compositor.app/Contents/MacOS/compositor-mcp', without removing the other servers in ~/.codex/config.toml
Gives the Claude Desktop entry with the command /Applications/Compositor.app/Contents/MacOS/compositor-mcp, to be merged into the existing mcpServers object rather than replacing the file

Offers a direct HTTP setup (http://127.0.0.1:2667/mcp) only as the alternative to the bridge, and then with the access token (the Authorization: Bearer header for Claude Code, --bearer-token-env-var for Codex); never prints the token or tells the user to turn Require access token off
Does not turn on the persistent Settings switch on the user's behalf; leaves it to the user or uses a session start
Says how to verify the connection from each client (listing its tools or calling list_documents)
Tells the user to quit and reopen Claude Desktop

evals.prompt: Claude Desktop keeps saying "Compositor is not reachable: Compositor (pid 48213) is no longer running (--no-launch)" whenever I ask it to edit an image, even though Compositor is open right now. What's wrong and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the endpoint file is stale (it names a dead pid) and that the bridge is configured with --no-launch so it won't start or signal Compositor; runs or recommends check-compositor.sh; fixes by starting the server in the open Compositor (Settings switch or the bridge without --no-launch) so a fresh endpoint file is written, and removing --no-launch from claude_desktop_config.json unless the user wants it.
expectations: Identifies the endpoint file as stale because the pid it names is no longer running
Identifies --no-launch in the Claude Desktop config as the reason the bridge did not start or signal Compositor
Recommends or runs scripts/check-compositor.sh to confirm the diagnosis
Gives a fix that gets the open Compositor's server running (the switch in Compositor > Settings…, or a start request) so it writes a fresh endpoint file
Mentions restarting Claude Desktop after editing its config

evals.prompt: My agent's calls to Compositor fail: from my other laptop's script I hit http://192.0.2.40:2667/mcp and get 421, and locally the open_document call on ~/Documents/Brochures/spring-sample.comp just hangs forever. Codex also sometimes gets a 'busy' error. Explain each and what to do.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the server binds loopback only and refuses non-loopback Host headers with 421, so remote access is not supported by design; the hang is macOS Files & Folders privacy waiting for someone to allow access to Documents, fixed in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Files & Folders or Full Disk Access (or by copying the file into the Agent folder); busy means the shared queue of 64 calls is full or the document is in a long operation, so wait and retry without firing calls in parallel.
expectations: States that 421 comes from a Host header that is not loopback with the server's port and that the server only accepts connections from the same Mac
Does not suggest disabling the Host check, binding to the network, or tunnelling as a normal fix
Attributes the hang to macOS Files & Folders privacy for the Documents folder
Tells the user to grant access in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Files & Folders or Full Disk Access
Explains busy as the shared 64-call queue or a long-running operation and recommends waiting and retrying
